---
title: "Who Said What"
---

::: {.ao-story}
Three voices speak in the mill: the one that built it, the one you wrote down, and yours. Only one of them is you. Learn to tell them apart, and you will know whose rule you are following and who can change it.
:::

::: {.quest-dialog}
- **Goal:** you will tell the system prompt, the instructions file and your own message apart, and know which you control and which only advise.
- **Before you start:** [The Context Window](the-context-window.html). This is an optional side quest.
- **Time:** about 15 minutes.
:::

When an agent follows a rule, it is fair to ask where that rule came from, because the answer tells you who can change it. The **harness** is the program around the model that runs tools and sends your text. It works with three common sources of rules, and they differ in who writes them, how long they last and whether anything enforces them.

## The three voices

| Voice | Who writes it | How long it lasts | Can you edit it? |
|---|---|---|---|
| **System prompt** | The harness | Sent ahead of the conversation on every request | Rarely; you can append or replace it with flags |
| **Instructions file** (`CLAUDE.md`) | You or your team | Loaded at the start of every session | Yes |
| **Your message** | You, now | This task | Yes |

In Claude Code, the system prompt is the set of instructions sent ahead of your conversation on every request: how to use tools, behave safely and format answers. Add to it with `--append-system-prompt` or replace it with `--system-prompt`.

`CLAUDE.md` is loaded at the start of every session **as a user message after the system prompt** (text the model receives in the user's role). It sits outside the system prompt. Output-style instructions (a setting that changes how the model words its replies) also sit outside it. Both arrive in the conversation as **system reminders** (notes the harness slips into the conversation).

## Rules you did not write

System reminders also carry the skills list, hook `additionalContext` (text a hook hands back for the harness to add to the conversation), notes about changed files and commit or pull-request attribution lines. A **hook** is a script the harness runs at set moments, such as just before a tool runs.

If the agent follows a rule you never wrote, for example adding a co-author line to commits, look at what the harness adds on its own first.

## Advice or enforcement

The instructions file is context that advises. Specific and short instructions are followed more consistently, and longer files use more context and reduce adherence.

To block an action regardless of what the model decides, use enforcement: a **PreToolUse hook** (a hook that runs at the point just before a tool runs, and is code that enforces the rule) or a deny rule (a settings rule that blocks a named action). Use enforcement for what must never happen.

::: {.panel-tabset group="companion"}

## Claude Code

Reads `CLAUDE.md`. If a project has only an `AGENTS.md` (and no `CLAUDE.md`, `.claude/CLAUDE.md` or `CLAUDE.local.md` in or above the working directory), it is read instead, from v2.1.277. To share one file, import it from `CLAUDE.md` with `@AGENTS.md`.

## OpenCode + Ollama

Check OpenCode's documentation for which instruction file names it loads, and in what order.

:::

## Lore

*Further reading. Optional.*

- [How Claude Code works](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/how-claude-code-works): Anthropic, docs. Why read: it describes what the harness adds to the conversation, useful for tracing where a behaviour came from.
- [How Claude remembers your project](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/memory): Anthropic, docs. Why read: it says CLAUDE.md is context that advises, which is why the instructions file sits at the "advises" end of this quest.
- [Hooks reference](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks): Anthropic, docs. Why read: it is the reference for the one control here that enforces, while the others ask; skim it to see what hooks can act on.
:::
